messages.subject: parseAndEval does not return
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I run a script on a remote Rserve like below:

connection.assign(".tmp.", script);
REXP r =
connection.parseAndEval("try(eval(parse(text=.tmp.)),silent=TRUE)");

The execution time is dependent on the given parameters. If my script runs
longer than ~30 min or so, the parseAndEval above returns never and my java
code is blocked forever. However on the server side, i see that the script
has finished running. Below 25-30 minutes execution time, it returns normal
and my java code does continue.

To debug the issue, i have started the Rserve in debug mode and added to
the last line a print("finished") statement. Then observed on the command
line:

[1] "finished"
Expression 1, error code: 0
expression(s) evaluated (Rerror=0).
String vector of length 1:
scalar string: "finished"
getStorageSize(0x2b7c938,type=16,len=1)
getStorageSize(0x2b7c908,type=9,len=5) = 12
= 16
result storage size = 4112 bytes
stored 0x2b7c938 at 0x7ffc25c1c018, 8 bytes
stored SEXP; length=16 (incl. DT_SEXP header)
OUT.sendRespData
HEAD DUMP [16]: 01 00 01 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 |................
BODY DUMP [16]: 0a 0c 00 00 22 08 00 00 62 69 74 74 69 00 01 01
 |...."...finished...
reply sent.

>From the last line, i understand that the Rserve sent the reply but then
what happens?

The Rserve runs on an Ubuntu 12.04 with java version "1.7.0_25" OpenJDK
Runtime Environment (IcedTea 2.3.10) (7u25-2.3.10-1ubuntu0.12.04.2).

What more information could i provide to understand this issue?

Best,Ilhami

messages.subject: Re: Running R script from java
messages.body_plain:
Peeyush,

On May 19, 2014, at 11:10 AM, peeyush <peeyush215 at gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Rosuda Developers,
> 
> I am using RServe.
> 
> I want to run R script (whole function) from java and want to source script to java. I am using this code:
> 
> import org.rosuda.REngine.REXP;
> import org.rosuda.REngine.REXPMismatchException;
> import org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection;
> import org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException;
>  
> public class SourcingRFile {
>     public static void main(String[] args) throws RserveException,
>             REXPMismatchException {
>         RConnection c = new RConnection();
>         // source the Palindrom function
>         c.eval("source(\"/home/peeyush/Desktop/Analysing_GeneMinerResults.R\")");
>  
>         // call the function. Return true
> Line 26: c.eval("GeneMiner()");
>     } 
> }
> 
> I am getting this error:
> 
> Exception in thread "main" org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: eval failed, request status: error code: 127
>     at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.eval(RConnection.java:234)
>     at de.bonn.limes.core.SourcingRFile.main(SourcingRFile.java:26)
> 
> Help me please, Thanks in advance.
> 

Please check the error in R - your code is failing there - either by looking at the server side or by using
c.eval("try(GeneMiner(), silent=TRUE)")
and looking at the result.

Note that the source() command is executed server-side, so the path you're using must be on the server.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Mac OS X 10.9 Mavericks - JGR and Java tips
messages.subject_clean: Mac OS X 10.9 Mavericks - JGR and Java tips
messages.body_plain:
Simon Urbanek <urbanek <at> research.att.com> writes:

> 
> Note that Mac OS X 10.9 upgrade creates a bit of a Java mess. If you try
to use Java it may be removed by the
> installer and crashes with CRAN binaries. Easiest to see is if you start
JGR and it just crashes - then you
> don't have the right Java installed. Unfortunately Apple's JAva updates
doesn't work if not run from
> their java command.
> 
> The trick is to get Apple's Java 1.6 - probably the easiest is to go to
Terminal and type
> 
> R CMD javareconf -n
> 
> which tries to configure Java for R and should trigger a prompt where the
OS is asking if you want to install
> Java 1.6 and you say yes. Once it downloads Java you can try to re-runt he
above and it should succeed.
> (Possibly just typing "java" may also do the trick, but checking it with R
is a good idea).
> 
> Cheers,
> Simon
> 
> 

Java 7 update 55 allows JGR to run, but JGR is crippled and often demands a
force quit.
